title: The frozen plain got a wind, the dark got a fire, and the buildings got shadows they stay attached to

verified.tests/render/frame_lab.tscn (new, 24 fra: TESTS PASSED; the same suite prints 9 named failures against the renderer it replaces (proved by restoring HEAD's game/view/render/** into a scratch copy)
verified.deep_night warm-pixel fraction: 0.0000 -> 0.0189 (a game about heat in the dark contained no warm pixel)
verified.deep_night_normal vs midday_normal lumin: 0.132 vs 0.428 — night is 3.2x darker and the lit city is the only warm thing in it
verified.tests/render/test_palette.gd night reado: 37 render tests pass; the rewritten test fails 3 assertions against HEAD's palette
verified.tests/render/render_perf.tscn, 1700 stru: collect 2133-2155 us, ground 652-670 us, entity draw 8361-8642 us, total 11137-11460 us vs 12000 us budget (was 1321 / 653 / 5670 / 7644)
verified.draw calls at 1700 structures with a dis: 14, unchanged from HEAD (the '8 draw calls' figure in the brief was already stale)

open: render_perf measured WITH a display on this shared box reports 13.9-16.9 ms and goes red, but HEAD~2 measures 10.9 ms on a quiet moment and the same 14 draw calls; llvmpipe plus four agents on four cores makes the wall clock meaningless here. INTEGRATOR must re-measure alone.

[P14] vfx: verified not the cause of the rectangles I chased (--no-vfx changes nothing), so nothing owed — but the vfx layer is installed in tests/render/frame_lab.tscn and --no-vfx is available there if they want a clean comparison.

[P21]/[P22]: every frame tools/run_visual.sh produces is buried under an undismissed narrative modal ('The Column Stopped Here', 'The First Night'). All seven harness shots show the panel, not the world. progress/shots/assault.png is left that way on purpose. The harness tour needs to dismiss or suppress modals between shot beats or the build has no usable screenshots of itself.

[P11]/[P01]: the ground shader reads snow accumulation from the grid's snow field; in the preview world it arrives at 0.04 of the cap, so the crust is currently carried almost entirely by the terrain kind's own drift rating. If the real map's snow_cap is set so depth stays that low, drifts will never deepen with a storm.

Buildings: 33 archetypes now have mass, a roof plane, a grounded silhouette shadow and lit windows that go out when they freeze, but the wall plane is still one flat gradient on most of them and only habitat/workshop/greenhouse have a roof that is not a rectangle. The next pass on the look is per-archetype wall material (stone vs steel vs timber), not more lighting.
